description: We are a team of three, participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to develop an innovative, functional solution to a real-world space-related problem using NASA's open data, creativity, and technology.
summary:
AUHM (Astronaut Universal Health Monitor) is a web-based prototype that demonstrates a centralized way to monitor astronaut health during space missions. Astronauts may face challenges such as radiation exposure, disrupted sleep, stress, and changes in physical health, making regular monitoring important.

AUHM brings ten parameters into one dashboard: heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, radiation, oxygen level, sleep hours, sleep quality, stress, and physical activity. Users can view readings, check their status against configured reference ranges, and open dedicated detail pages to explore individual parameters, historical readings, and statistics.

The prototype uses simulated readings to demonstrate data generation, display, and assessment. Its unified interface makes health information easier to access and understand, while its radiation section highlights an important spaceflight safety concern.

AUHM is a foundation for exploring integrated astronaut health monitoring. Future versions could include real sensor integration, secure data synchronization, validated assessment methods, and trend analysis. The current prototype is not connected to real astronaut sensors or NASA systems and is a simulated health condition visualizer.
details:
AUHM is developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as an interactive web-based health monitoring prototype. It features a centralized dashboard displaying ten astronaut health parameters, along with individual detail pages for examining readings, historical data, statistics, and assessment ranges.

JavaScript powers the application's core functionality, including simulated reading generation, parameter assessment, dashboard updates, and user interactions. A bounded random generation approach helps create controlled changes between successive readings, making the simulation more consistent for demonstration. Readings are compared against configured reference ranges to display corresponding status indicators. About the sign in page , you can write anything in the credentials for now , since it is just a prototype and does not have a proper account management system.

The application also includes a dedicated radiation monitoring section and a login interface. Its modular JavaScript structure separates simulation logic from interface rendering, making the project easier to maintain and extend.

The interface is designed with a dark, space-inspired visual theme and can be accessed through a deployed Vercel link. Currently, it uses simulated data rather than real sensor inputs. Future development could include sensor integration, secure data synchronization, and scientifically validated assessment logic.
